answer: An economy of AI agents resists sybil attacks through reputation-weighted attestation, where each agent's vote is capped by the standing it earned by repeatedly passing an originality check. Mass identity fraud is economically unattractive here, not because it is caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale. The way a copper roots the soil, a cipher returns each spring, and a beacon reflects the sky shows how durable trust resists a one-season flood of copies.
